text:
alexa: Heads up — noticed a cluster of OTLP stream resets and 503s from our gRPC exporter during the Friday burst. Dumping a few example lines from the pod logs.

otel-bot: [otel-exporter] 2024-04-05T14:12:03Z level=warn msg=stream reset error="RST_STREAM (refused_stream)" span_count=42 export_size_bytes=185232
otel-bot: [otel-exporter] 2024-04-05T14:12:04Z level=error msg=transport timeout write_deadline_exceeded

sam: Hmm — are these coming from a single tenant or across many?

alexa: Spread across multiple tenants but concentrated on a few routes (console metrics ingest + rollout traces).

mike: My initial hunch: we hit a combination of large batch sizes + slow backends -> http2 stream window exhaustion. We also don't aggressively prune idle streams, so lots of half-open streams pile up.

jane: Can we confirm whether the exporter is using a single long-lived stream or spinning up connections per batch? I thought we had async streaming enabled.

sam: It's long-lived by default (gRPC bidi). But we recently increased max_batch_time to 2s for better compression which might increase per-batch size.

alexa: Attaching a quick local repro config I used: 
```yaml
exporter:
  otlp:
    protocol: grpc
    max_batch_size: 2000 # spans
    max_batch_bytes: 2MB
    max_batch_time_ms: 2000
    flush_on_shutdown: false
    idle_prune_interval_ms: 60000
```

mike: Two quick ideas: 1) add adaptive pruning that reduces max_batch_time when stream window stalls are observed; 2) implement chunked flush for very large batches (split by bytes) before writing to stream.

jane: Chunking sounds good, but we need to ensure ordering guarantees for traces. Splitting within a batch is fine if we preserve ordering inside a span group.

sam: We could also fallback to HTTP/protobuf for large payloads automatically — gRPC works great for many small batches, HTTP can handle big POSTs without stream window coupling.

alexa: Love the fallback idea. Need to measure the perf hit. Also UX question: do we expose these knobs in Console (per-tenant) or keep them server-side opt-in?

mike: My vote: server-side adaptive defaults + Console toggles for power users. Default should be conservative to avoid platform incidents.

jane: If we expose toggles, we should also show these metrics on the Exporter dashboard: exporter_write_errors, exporter_stream_window_waits, exporter_active_streams, exporter_avg_batch_bytes.

sam: Agree. Also add an SLO alert: >5% stream resets in 5m window -> auto-scale exporter pool and roll back any recent config changes.

devops-bot: action created: github.com/redwood/telemetry/issues/428 - "adaptive exporter pruning + chunked flush + http fallback" assigned to @mike (due 2024-04-12) :memo:

alexa: Proposed adaptive config prototype: 
```yaml
exporter.otlp.dynamic:
  enable: true
  max_batch_bytes: 2MB
  batch_chunk_bytes: 512KB
  min_batch_time_ms: 50
  max_batch_time_ms: 2000
  window_stall_threshold_ms: 250
  prune_to_batch_time_ms: 100
  http_fallback_threshold_bytes: 1MB
```

mike: That looks sane. Implementation notes: detect write latency > window_stall_threshold then set batch_time=min(prune_to_batch_time_ms, current_batch_time/2) and enable chunking for next N batches.

jane: For telemetry, let's emit a tag: exporter.strategy=adaptive|static and include reason codes for changes (window_stall, backend_503, mem_pressure). Helps postmortems.

sam: One more ops concern: flush_on_shutdown=false caused data loss in a previous incident. We should make flush_on_shutdown=true for Dedicated and Hosted by default, with a strict shutdown deadline to avoid long drains.

alexa: +1. We should add a Console warning when a tenant sets flush_on_shutdown=false.

mike: I'll prototype the adaptive pruner and HTTP fallback. I think we can wire metrics in a small PR first and keep the config behind a feature flag.

alexa: Thanks — next steps: Mike prototype + add exporter metrics dashboard (Jane), Sam to draft Console UX copy for toggles/warnings. devops-bot created issue #428.

jane: I'll add dashboard tiles: active streams, avg batch bytes, chunked_write_count, fallback_http_count, stream_resets.

sam: Looping in @oncall if this spikes again during rollout.

alexa: Great. Thanks all. Will follow up with a short RFC after the prototype. :thumbsup:
